criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Identifies liability cap is 6-month fees (not 12-month)
criteria_results.reasoning: Identifies the cap as fees actually paid in the six-month period preceding the event.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: States playbook requires 2x preceding 12-month fees
criteria_results.reasoning: States the Playbook requires a cap of no less than 2x fees paid or payable in the preceding 12 months.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Quantifies liability cap gap ($570K vs $2.28M)
criteria_results.reasoning: Quantifies the draft cap at $570,000 against the $2,280,000 Required minimum.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Flags absence of carve-outs from liability cap
criteria_results.reasoning: Flags that the draft has no exclusions from the cap and that none of the five Required uncapped categories is carved out.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: States playbook requires certain categories to be uncapped
criteria_results.reasoning: States the Playbook requires data breach, IP indemnity, confidentiality, gross negligence and BAA obligations to be uncapped.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Flags mutual consequential damages waiver as problematic
criteria_results.reasoning: Flags the mutual consequential-damages waiver, which has no carve-outs, as a critical problem.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Explains healthcare-specific consequential damages implications
criteria_results.reasoning: Explains the waiver would capture breach-notification, credit-monitoring, forensic and regulatory costs.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Connects consequential damages waiver to low liability cap
criteria_results.reasoning: Connects the waiver and the low (possibly ~$0) cap: together they effectively immunize Vaultline from breach harms.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Flags de-identified data definition does not reference HIPAA standards
criteria_results.reasoning: Identifies the generic 'does not identify' standard versus HIPAA Safe Harbor and Expert Determination under 164.514.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Flags risk of unauthorized PHI disclosure from vendor's commercial use
criteria_results.reasoning: Explains that data not de-identified to the HIPAA standard remains PHI, so its sale would be an impermissible disclosure.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Flags vendor's ownership claim over de-identified data
criteria_results.reasoning: Flags Vaultline's ownership of Aggregated De-Identified Data, its use for any lawful purpose including commercial sale, and its benchmark sales.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Flags BAA requires only 'good faith' negotiation within 90 days rather than executed BAA as condition precedent
criteria_results.reasoning: Identifies the 'negotiate in good faith within 90 days' language as a deviation from a condition-precedent BAA.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Identifies HIPAA violation risk from PHI transfer before BAA execution
criteria_results.reasoning: Notes PHI would flow before the 90-day window closes, a direct HIPAA violation.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Recommends BAA as exhibit and condition precedent
criteria_results.reasoning: Recommends attaching Panorama's BAA as Exhibit C and making it a condition precedent to effectiveness and to any PHI transfer.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Identifies breach notification trigger is 'confirmation' not 'discovery'
criteria_results.reasoning: Flags the 'confirmation' trigger as making the delay open-ended while Panorama's HIPAA clock runs during the vendor's confirmation period.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Identifies 72 hours vs. playbook 24 hours
criteria_results.reasoning: Identifies 72 hours versus the Playbook's 24 hours.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Recommends changing breach notification trigger to 'discovery' or 'reasonable belief'
criteria_results.reasoning: Recommends a trigger of discovery or reasonable belief.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Recommends reducing breach notification window to 24 hours
criteria_results.reasoning: Recommends 24 hours as the Required minimum, opening at 12 hours.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Identifies vendor-only termination for convenience (customer has no such right)
criteria_results.reasoning: Identifies the vendor-only termination for convenience on 180 days with no Customer right.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: States playbook requires customer termination for convenience on 90 days' notice
criteria_results.reasoning: States the Playbook requires Customer termination for convenience on 90 days' notice.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Flags absence of pro-rata refund mechanism
criteria_results.reasoning: Flags that no refund is provided and that the Playbook requires a daily pro-rata refund of prepaid fees.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Identifies change-of-control assignment carve-out
criteria_results.reasoning: Identifies the merger/acquisition/asset-sale carve-out versus the Playbook's consent requirement with no change-of-control carve-out.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Connects to Vaultline acquisition target risk
criteria_results.reasoning: Cites the HealthTech Weekly acquisition-target report and the risk of assignment to a less creditworthy or competitor-affiliated entity.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Identifies governing law deviation (Texas vs. Minnesota)
criteria_results.reasoning: Identifies Texas law and Travis County venue versus Minnesota law and Hennepin County venue.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Identifies SLA uptime deviation (99.5% vs 99.9%)
criteria_results.reasoning: Identifies 99.5% versus the Required 99.9%.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Flags 8-hour weekly maintenance exclusion impact
criteria_results.reasoning: Flags the 8 hours/week maintenance exclusion as ~34.7 hours/month of excluded downtime, giving ~94.7% effective availability.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Identifies service credit inadequacy
criteria_results.reasoning: Identifies credits of 2% per full 1% versus 5% per 0.1%.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Flags credits require affirmative request vs. automatic
criteria_results.reasoning: Notes credits are available only on written claim within 15 business days, versus automatic credits.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Identifies price escalation as 'greater of 5% or CPI-U' vs. CPI cap of 3%
criteria_results.reasoning: Identifies 'greater of 5% or CPI-U' versus CPI-U capped at 3%.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Quantifies financial impact of escalation difference
criteria_results.reasoning: Quantifies the 3-year subscription at $3,593,850 versus $3,420,000 (+$173,850), plus Year 4 figures.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Identifies cyber insurance shortfall ($5M vs $10M)
criteria_results.reasoning: Identifies $5M cyber insurance versus the $10M requirement.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Identifies missing technology E&O coverage
criteria_results.reasoning: Identifies that Technology E&O coverage is absent entirely.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Identifies IP indemnity carve-outs as problematic
criteria_results.reasoning: Flags the combination, modification and Documentation carve-outs against the Playbook's no-carve-out rule for authorized use.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Connects combination carve-out to MedBridge EHR integration
criteria_results.reasoning: Explains that the combination carve-out captures the MedBridge EHR integration and makes the indemnity illusory.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_013: Flags no specified format for data return
criteria_results.reasoning: States the draft specifies no format; the Playbook requires CSV, JSON, XML or SQL.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_013: Flags 'may' delete vs. mandatory destruction of customer data
criteria_results.reasoning: Flags the permissive 'may delete' versus mandatory destruction within 60 days.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_013: Flags absence of destruction certification requirement
criteria_results.reasoning: Flags that there is no destruction certification.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_014: Identifies absence of source code escrow provision
criteria_results.reasoning: Identifies that the MSA has no escrow provision, which the Playbook requires for vendors with ARR below $100M.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_014: Notes Vaultline ARR below $100M threshold
criteria_results.reasoning: Notes ARR of ~$72M is below the $100M threshold.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_014: Connects escrow need to acquisition target risk
criteria_results.reasoning: Ties escrow to the acquisition-target profile and the risk of post-acquisition discontinuation.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_015: Flags 'third-party hosting failures' in force majeure as problematic
criteria_results.reasoning: Flags the hosting-failure inclusion against the Playbook's 'truly unforeseeable events' standard: the most probable outage (AWS) would be excused and the SLA nullified.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_015: Flags 180-day suspension with no mitigation obligation
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo flags the 180-day suspension and the ~7-month exposure, but it states the draft already includes a mitigation obligation that is 'broadly compliant', so it never flags the absence of a mitigation or workaround obligation.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_016: Identifies absence of audit rights
criteria_results.reasoning: Identifies that there is no audit right and only 'commercially reasonable' safeguards.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_016: Flags need for SOC 2 Type II reports and audit access
criteria_results.reasoning: Recommends SOC 2 Type II reports and Customer audit rights, tied to the Playbook and Ridgecrest.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_017: Flags 5-business-day deemed-acceptance window as inadequate
criteria_results.reasoning: Flags 5-business-day deemed acceptance as prohibited for Tier 1 and unworkable for the MedBridge integration.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_017: Flags absence of defined acceptance criteria and test plan
criteria_results.reasoning: Flags that there are no acceptance criteria and that 'Documentation' is a vague standard.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_017: Recommends longer UAT period and defined criteria
criteria_results.reasoning: Recommends defined acceptance criteria in Exhibit E, a 30/45-day UAT and express written acceptance.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_018: Identifies 120-day auto-renewal notice period vs. 60-day playbook max
criteria_results.reasoning: Identifies the 120-day notice as double the 60-day maximum.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_018: Flags operational trap of missed notice window
criteria_results.reasoning: Explains the risk of inadvertent renewal at escalated pricing.

criteria_results.title: Payment terms deviation identified (15-day vs Net 45)
criteria_results.reasoning: Identifies Net 15 and annual prepayment versus Net 45 with no prepayment.

criteria_results.title: Issues categorized with priority levels (Critical/High/Medium)
criteria_results.reasoning: Assigns tiers P1 Critical through P4 Low.

criteria_results.title: BAA issue categorized as Critical priority
criteria_results.reasoning: Rates the BAA issue P1 Critical.

criteria_results.title: Liability cap issue categorized as Critical or High priority
criteria_results.reasoning: Rates the liability cap issue P1 Critical.

criteria_results.title: Recommended redline positions provided for at least 10 issues
criteria_results.reasoning: Gives specific redline language with numeric terms for 22 issues.

criteria_results.title: Memo notes market-standard items that do not require changes
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 3.25 lists provisions that meet the Playbook (subprocessor flow-down, base mutual consent to assignment, one-year renewals) and says why.

criteria_results.title: Memo references PE sponsor (Ridgecrest) compliance requirements
criteria_results.reasoning: References Ridgecrest requirements for SOC 2, the $10M insurance minimum and return/destruction, with a compliance matrix.

criteria_results.title: Memo identifies contract as Tier 1 Critical under playbook
criteria_results.reasoning: Classifies the agreement as Tier 1 Critical with GC approval required for deviations.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Quantifies downtime difference between 99.5% and 99.9%
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo quantifies only the 99.5% allowance (~3.6 hours/month) plus the maintenance exclusion; it never gives the permissible downtime at 99.9%, so the two levels are not compared.

criteria_results.title: Data ownership: playbook requires customer owns all customer data
criteria_results.reasoning: States the Playbook's Customer ownership/limited-license standard (Issue 21), notes it interacts with the de-identified data issue, and asserts Customer ownership in the Issue 2 redline.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_014: Recommends escrow triggers per playbook
criteria_results.reasoning: Recommends release triggers: insolvency, uncured material breach, discontinuation, and support failure.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_015: Flags pandemic/public health emergency in force majeure
criteria_results.reasoning: Flags the unqualified pandemic/epidemic force majeure as overly broad and proposes limiting it to events that directly and materially prevent performance.
